key_insight: RetroThinker lets a streaming SpeechLLM revise its own reasoning during inference, improving reasoning accuracy without breaking real-time interaction constraints.
engineering_relevance: This matters for low-latency spoken AI systems because it offers a practical way to recover reasoning quality while preserving the speed and paralinguistic benefits of end-to-end speech models.
method: Curated retrospective-thinking data for supervised fine-tuning (SFT)
Length-based direct preference optimization (DPO) to favor useful early revisions
Enabled the Moshi SpeechLLM to self-verify and forward-correct chain-of-thought steps during streaming inference
evidence_signal: On GSM8K, the abstract reports an 11% absolute accuracy gain at comparable latency versus non-retrospective baselines.
watch_item: The approach adds training and inference complexity, so its real-world latency and stability may depend on how well retrospective revisions are controlled in streaming deployment.
paper_title: RetroThinker: Enabling Retrospective Thinking in Speech LLMs
